headline: A strong night on Wall Street lifted most of your portfolio today, but Pilbara Minerals and GXAI remain the standout drags — the NRL Grand Final was a thriller, with the Roosters edging the Knights 19-18.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced +1.5% at today's close, a rare green day for a stock that's been under sustained pressure. Lithium spot prices remain deeply depressed — analysts are tracking sellers targeting 80,000 yuan per tonne, well below levels that make most Australian lithium miners profitable. Today's move is a small relief, not a turning point.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed up +1.3% today, riding a broader tech tailwind from last night's strong NASDAQ session (+2.3%). The ETF holds global AI-related companies, so a big night for US tech names flows through here. The position is still down nearly 20% overall, but the long-term AI thematic is very much intact.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two rose +1.3% last night on the NASDAQ. GTA 6 buzz continues to build — there's active news around the PC port and modding community engagement, keeping the brand in headlines. With GTA 6 still ahead, the long-term revenue story for Take-Two remains compelling.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged up +0.6% last night. There's a note in the news cycle that MSFT is down about 7.6% since its last earnings report — the market is digesting some post-earnings caution — but the underlying automation and AI cloud business remains strong. A quiet, steady session.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose +0.5% last night. Interestingly, Google Cloud revenue reportedly more than doubled yet the stock has faced headwinds recently — the market seems to be weighing AI competition risks against genuinely strong cloud numbers. The position is currently down about 11% overall, but Google's fundamentals remain solid.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG closed up +0.67% today, following the broader ASX 200 higher (+0.8%). This diversified ETF holds a mix of Aussie and global shares, so a solid day across both markets gave it a nice lift.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up +0.65% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's strong S&P 500 performance (+1.6%). This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so when Wall Street has a big night, VTS follows suit.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF)
movers.note: DHHF ticked up +0.48% at today's close, in line with the market. A steady, uneventful session for this globally diversified growth ETF — exactly what you want from a core long-term holding.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was essentially flat today (+0.07%), which is fairly typical — emerging markets (think China, India, Brazil) tend to move on their own rhythms and didn't have a strong catalyst today. The position is down about 6% overall, but emerging markets exposure is a long-term play.

watch_today.title: PLS: A green day, but lithium's structural pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced +1.5% today, but the news is sobering — lithium prices are crashing again, with sellers targeting 80,000 yuan per tonne. That level is well below what most Aussie lithium miners need to be profitable. PLS is down over 60% on your cost base. The long-term lithium demand story (EVs, batteries) is still real, but the timeline for a price recovery has stretched out significantly. Hold for now — selling at these levels locks in a large loss with no recovery upside.

watch_today.title: GXAI: AI tailwind today, but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: GXAI had a nice +1.3% session today off the back of a strong NASDAQ night. The position is still down nearly 20% overall. Nothing has broken with the AI thematic — if anything, the narrative around AI regulation, Chinese AI delays, and ongoing US tech dominance suggests the sector has a long runway. Sit tight and let the thesis play out.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype keeps building — long-term story intact
watch_today.detail: Take-Two rose +1.3% last night and GTA 6 is generating steady buzz, including Australian-specific news around a missing feature and active modding on the PC port. As a long-term hold, Take-Two's pipeline is as strong as it's ever been. No reason to touch this — just let it run.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision risk: IMF warns more hikes may be needed
watch_today.detail: The IMF has publicly told the RBA to be ready to raise interest rates further, even after 125 basis points (1.25%) of hikes already this year. Meanwhile, inflation is still running hot enough that the RBA is under real pressure. Higher rates are a headwind for growth stocks and property — worth keeping an eye on your VDHG and DHHF holdings, which have some rate-sensitive exposure.

watch_today.title: Wall Street had a big night — your US-linked holdings all nudged higher
watch_today.detail: The NASDAQ surged +2.3% and the S&P 500 rose +1.6% last night. That's flowing through into your GXAI, VTS, VDHG, MSFT, GOOG and TTWO positions. No single stock catalyst — it was a broad risk-on session. Good backdrop heading into the weekend.

watch_today.title: Gold hitting record highs — worth watching macro backdrop
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped nearly +3% last night to US$3,639/oz. Gold typically surges when investors are nervous about inflation, geopolitical risk, or currency instability — and all three are present right now (Iran tensions, US economic data disputes, RBA rate uncertainty). You don't hold gold directly, but it's a signal the macro environment is uncertain. Keep your diversified ETF positions (VDHG, DHHF) and don't make reactive moves.

world.summary: Iran's economic crisis deepens under US sanctions, the UN warns of worsening hunger in the Middle East, and Trump is demanding a probe into US economic data. A busy and concerning week on the global stage.

stories.title: A 'Silent War' Grips Iran as Its Economy Strains Under US Blockade
stories.why_it_matters: The WSJ reports that Iran is experiencing what insiders are calling a 'silent war' — not from missiles, but from the crushing weight of US economic sanctions. The Iranian economy is under severe strain, with the currency collapsing and ordinary Iranians struggling to afford basics. Iran's envoy is simultaneously urging students to push back on Western narratives. The situation is escalating diplomatically, and any further destabilisation of Iran could affect oil markets and broader Middle East stability — which matters for energy prices globally.

stories.title: UN Warns Hunger Will Deepen in the Middle East as War, Fuel Costs and Aid Cuts Collide
stories.why_it_matters: The United Nations is warning that hunger across the Middle East is set to worsen significantly, with three forces colliding: ongoing armed conflicts, surging fuel costs that make food transport and production more expensive, and deep cuts to international aid programs. This is a humanitarian crisis building in real time, affecting millions of civilians caught between geopolitical disputes they have no control over. For Australians, this is a reminder of how connected global food security and energy costs are to everyday prices here at home.

stories.title: Trump Demands Probe Into 'Fake' Economic Figures
stories.why_it_matters: Donald Trump is demanding an investigation into what he's calling 'fake' US economic figures — suggesting the official economic data being published by government agencies isn't accurate or is being manipulated. This is a significant escalation in distrust of US institutions. If the credibility of American economic data comes into question, it creates uncertainty for global markets that rely on those numbers to make decisions. Last night's gold price surge to nearly US$3,640/oz may partly reflect this kind of institutional uncertainty.

stories.title: Tanker Rates Face Two-Year Decline Regardless of Middle East Conflict
stories.why_it_matters: Industry body BIMCO is forecasting that shipping tanker rates — the cost of moving oil around the world by sea — will fall for two years regardless of what happens in the Middle East. The reason: a glut of new tankers coming into service is outpacing demand. Cheaper tanker rates are generally good for the global economy (lower transport costs for oil and goods), but bad news for shipping companies. It also signals that the market doesn't expect a major escalation in the Strait of Hormuz to disrupt trade routes long-term.

markets.summary: A strong night on Wall Street — the NASDAQ surged over 2% and the S&P 500 had its best night in weeks. The ASX followed suit today, closing up 0.8%. Gold hit near-record highs above US$3,600, while oil slipped slightly. The Aussie dollar edged a touch higher.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session on the ASX today, up 0.8%, lifted by the strong Wall Street lead from last night.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: The S&P 500 had a strong night last session, gaining 1.6% — a broad-based rally across most sectors.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ surged 2.3% last night, led by tech names. Good news for your GOOG, MSFT, TTWO and GXAI holdings.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil slipped slightly, down 0.7%. No major supply shock — markets are relatively calm on the energy front despite Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged nearly 3% last night to above US$3,600 — investors are piling into safe-haven assets amid geopolitical uncertainty and inflation concerns.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged slightly higher. At 66.5 US cents, it's still below long-term averages — a weaker AUD boosts the value of your US-denominated holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD.

politics.summary: Australia's domestic debate is dominated by gas policy, the RBA's interest rate path, and fallout from COP31 climate negotiations. The Victorian state election is also in focus heading into the weekend.

stories.title: Australia's New Gas Reservation Policy: Will It Actually Keep Prices Low?
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government's new gas reservation policy requires gas producers to set aside a portion of output for domestic use before exporting it — the idea being to keep Australian gas prices affordable for households and businesses. The Conversation is asking whether it'll actually work, given the complexity of gas markets and long-term export contracts already locked in. For Gold Coast households, gas and electricity prices have been a major cost-of-living pressure, so this policy matters directly.

stories.title: IMF Tells RBA to Stand Ready for More Rate Hikes, Even After 125bp of Tightening This Year
stories.why_it_matters: The International Monetary Fund has publicly urged the Reserve Bank of Australia to be prepared to raise interest rates again, warning that inflation risks haven't gone away — even after the RBA has already hiked rates by 1.25 percentage points this year. That's a big deal: more rate hikes mean higher mortgage repayments for millions of Australians. At the same time, some economists are arguing the RBA has gone too far and should cut rates immediately. The RBA is caught between two camps, and a decision either way will ripple through housing, spending, and your investments.

stories.title: COP31 'Failure' Reveals Depth of Australia's Climate Policy Problems
stories.why_it_matters: COP31 — the UN's annual global climate summit, this year held in Australia — has drawn sharp criticism, with The Saturday Paper arguing it exposed serious failures in Labor's climate policy under Albanese and Climate Change Minister Bowen. Critics from both left and right are unhappy: progressives say Australia didn't push hard enough on emissions reductions, while conservatives like The Spectator argue the government went too far. For Australian investors, climate policy direction affects energy companies, infrastructure spending, and the transition away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: Everything You Need to Know About the Victorian Election
stories.why_it_matters: Victoria is heading to a state election and the AFR has published a full explainer. The key issues are cost of living, infrastructure spending, and energy policy — themes that mirror the federal debate. Victorian election outcomes can influence policy settings on housing, planning, and energy that have knock-on effects for businesses and investors with exposure to the state.

ai.summary: It's Black Friday in the AI world too — Google and Adobe are offering subscription discounts, while OpenAI and Anthropic are holding firm on pricing. Meanwhile, Chinese AI developers are facing delays that give Western companies some breathing room, and the AI regulation debate is heating up globally.

stories.title: Google and Adobe Cut AI Subscription Prices for Black Friday; OpenAI and Anthropic Hold Firm
stories.why_it_matters: Google (Gemini) and Adobe are running Black Friday discounts on their AI subscriptions, making it a good time to try paid AI tools at a lower price. OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude) are not discounting — suggesting they're confident enough in demand to hold their prices. For anyone curious about upgrading their AI tools, this week is worth a look. For your GOOG holding, it's a minor positive signal that Google is actively competing for AI subscribers.

stories.title: Chinese AI Developers Face Delays, Giving Western Rivals Breathing Room
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI companies — which have been racing to catch up with OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic — are reportedly hitting regulatory and technical delays in rolling out their latest models. That gives US-based AI leaders more time to cement their lead in enterprise customers and developers. This is a tailwind for your GOOG holding and for GXAI, which invests in global AI companies heavily weighted toward US leaders.

stories.title: AI at US Retailers Is Drawing Calls for Guardrails
stories.why_it_matters: As AI tools are being rapidly adopted by US retailers — think personalised pricing, automated customer service, inventory management — The Guardian reports growing calls for regulation and consumer protections. Critics say AI is being deployed faster than the rules to govern it, creating risks around bias, pricing manipulation, and job losses. This is a tension that will define the next few years of AI adoption across all industries, and is worth watching for anyone holding AI-focused investments like GXAI.

stories.title: Global AI Regulation: What Companies Need to Know About the EU AI Act and Beyond
stories.why_it_matters: Legal 500 has published a comprehensive guide to how AI regulation is unfolding across the EU (via the EU AI Act), the US, UK, China, and other jurisdictions. The key takeaway: compliance is becoming a serious cost and risk for any company using AI at scale. The EU AI Act is the world's most comprehensive AI law so far, banning certain high-risk uses outright and requiring audits for others. For AI-exposed investments, regulatory compliance costs are worth monitoring — they could squeeze margins for smaller players while entrenching big tech companies that can afford legal teams.

sport.summary: NRL Grand Final delivered a classic thriller — Roosters over Knights 19-18. AFL off-season is in full swing with trades, signings, and weddings making headlines.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters Defeat Knights 19-18 in a Heart-Stopper
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL premiership, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium in one of the tightest Grand Finals in recent memory. One point in it at the final whistle — it doesn't get much closer than that. A huge result for the Roosters faithful and a heartbreaking one for Newcastle, who came agonisingly close to their first title in years.

stories.title: AFL: Premiership Winner Departs Collingwood Immediately After Five Years
stories.why_it_matters: A Collingwood premiership player has departed the club immediately after five seasons, with the AFL world paying tribute. The exit comes in the thick of the off-season trade period, with clubs reshaping their lists ahead of 2027. No replacement has been named yet, and this could signal a broader rebuild at the Pies.

stories.title: AFL Off-Season: Western Bulldogs Sign VFL Gun, Hawks Lose Father-Son to Interstate Rival
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade and free agency period is heating up. The Western Bulldogs have signed a 25-year-old VFL (Victoria's development league) gun, adding depth to their list. Meanwhile, an interstate club has successfully poached a Hawthorn father-son prospect — a significant move given the sentimental and strategic weight of father-son selections in AFL. The off-season reshuffle is well underway as clubs position for 2027.
